MeasureTheory.combine_estimates₁.statement:
Let $A > 0$, $p_0 \in (0, q_0]$, $p_1 \in (0, q_1]$, $t \in (0,1)$, $p_0 < p_1$, $q_0 
e q_1$, $p^{-1} = (1-t)p_0^{-1} + t p_1^{-1}$, $q^{-1} = (1-t)q_0^{-1} + t q_1^{-1}$ (exponents in $[0,\infty]$). Let $f \in L^p(\mu)$, suppose $T$ is subadditive under truncation of $f$ with constant $A$ with respect to $
u$ ($\mathrm{SubadditiveTrunc}\ T\ A\ f\ 
u$), $T$ has weak type $(p_1, q_1)$ with constant $C_1$ and weak type $(p_0, q_0)$ with constant $C_0$ (from $\mu$ to $
u$), $T$ preserves a.e. strong measurability on $L^p$, $C_0, C_1 > 0$, $0 < \|f\|_{L^p(\mu)} < \infty$, and $\mathrm{spf}$ is the scaled power function $\mathrm{ChoiceScale.spf\_ch}(\dots)$ determined by these data. Then $$\|T f\|_{L^q(
u)} \le 2A \cdot q^{1/q} \cdot \Big(\mathbf{1}[q_1 < \infty]\,|q - q_1|^{-1} + \mathbf{1}[q_0 < \infty]\,|q - q_0|^{-1}\Big)^{1/q} \cdot C_0^{1-t}\, C_1^{t}\, \|f\|_{L^p(\mu)},$$ where $\mathbf{1}[\cdot]$ is $1$ if the condition holds and $0$ otherwise, and $|q-q_i|^{-1}$ is computed in the reals (with $0^{-1} = 0$) and then viewed in $[0,\infty]$.

MeasureTheory.combine_estimates₀.statement:
Let $A > 0$, $p_0 \in (0, q_0]$, $p_1 \in (0, q_1]$, $t \in (0,1)$, $p_0 < p_1$, $q_0 
e q_1$, $p^{-1} = (1-t)p_0^{-1} + t p_1^{-1}$, $q^{-1} = (1-t)q_0^{-1} + t q_1^{-1}$ (exponents in $[0,\infty]$). Let $f \in L^p(\mu)$, suppose $T$ is subadditive under truncation of $f$ with constant $A$ with respect to $
u$ ($\mathrm{SubadditiveTrunc}\ T\ A\ f\ 
u$), $T$ has weak type $(p_1, q_1)$ with constant $C_1$ and weak type $(p_0, q_0)$ with constant $C_0$ (from $\mu$ to $
u$), $T$ preserves a.e. strong measurability on $L^p$, $C_0, C_1 > 0$, $0 < \|f\|_{L^p(\mu)} < \infty$, and $\mathrm{spf}$ is the scaled power function $\mathrm{ChoiceScale.spf\_ch}(\dots)$ determined by these data. Then $$\int \|T f(x)\|^{q}\, d
u(x) \le (2A)^{q}\, q \cdot \Big(\mathbf{1}[q_1 < \infty]\,|q - q_1|^{-1} + \mathbf{1}[q_0 < \infty]\,|q - q_0|^{-1}\Big) \cdot C_0^{(1-t)q}\, C_1^{tq}\, \|f\|_{L^p(\mu)}^{q},$$ where $\mathbf{1}[\cdot]$ is $1$ if the condition holds and $0$ otherwise, and $|q-q_i|^{-1}$ is computed in the reals (with $0^{-1} = 0$) and then viewed in $[0,\infty]$.

MeasureTheory.exists_hasStrongType_real_.statement:
Let $A > 0$, $p_0 \in (0, q_0]$, $p_1 \in (0, q_1]$, $q_0 
e q_1$, $t \in (0,1)$, $C_0, C_1 > 0$, $p^{-1} = (1-t)/p_0 + t/p_1$, $q^{-1} = (1-t)/q_0 + t/q_1$ (exponents in $[0,\infty]$); suppose $T$ is subadditive under truncation of $f$ with constant $A$ with respect to $
u$ ($\mathrm{SubadditiveTrunc}\ T\ A\ f\ 
u$), $T$ has weak type $(p_0, q_0)$ with constant $C_0$ and weak type $(p_1, q_1)$ with constant $C_1$ (from $\mu$ to $
u$), $T$ preserves a.e. strong measurability on $L^p$, and $f \in L^p(\mu)$. Then $$\|T f\|_{L^q(
u)} \le c \cdot q^{1/q} \cdot \Big(\mathbf{1}[q_1 < \infty]\,|q - q_1|^{-1} + \mathbf{1}[q_0 < \infty]\,|q - q_0|^{-1}\Big)^{1/q} \cdot C_0^{1-t}\, C_1^{t}\, \|f\|_{L^p(\mu)},$$ where $c = 1$ if $p_0 = p_1$ and $c = 2A$ otherwise, $\mathbf{1}[\cdot]$ is $1$ if the condition holds and $0$ otherwise, and $|q-q_i|^{-1}$ is computed in the reals (with $0^{-1} = 0$). This is the main estimate of the real interpolation theorem, combining the cases $p_0 
e p_1$ and $p_0 = p_1$.
